name: provenance
why: Included by the tools whose payload IS a symbol. gh#11 lets memberdef hold a row
the tree-sitter parser recovered rather than one doxygen documented, and marks it
`provenance: 'ast'`. Without this text the mark is disclosure nobody reads, and the
mistake it prevents is specific and silent: a recovered row has an EMPTY brief, so a
model that never learned the field exists reads that as 'this function is
undocumented' when the truth is 'doxygen could not parse this file at all'. Those two
readings lead to opposite actions — the first says the code is fine and the docs are
thin, the second says the INDEX is thin and its counts should not be trusted.
Measured on mbedtls: 2,527 of 4,206 indexed functions are parser-recovered, so on a
target in that state the field is the majority case, not an edge case. On entropic it
is 2 of 2,058. The field is ABSENT on a doxygen row precisely because that is the norm
and wire elision drops it — stating the default here is what makes the absence
readable instead of ambiguous.
Cut 2026-08-11 for the fixed-prompt budget. The dropped sentence explained that on a
dossier `provenance: 'ast'` beside a NON-EMPTY brief is not a contradiction — doxygen
documented the header declaration while the parser recovered the definition it could
not read.
ROUND 2, 2026-08-11. Cut to the two readings that change an action: what an absent
field means, and what an empty brief on an `ast` row means. Moved here: the usual
cause (code behind an unsatisfied preprocessor guard), the enumeration of what such a
row lacks (no brief, no parameters, no requirement tags — implied by 'the parser
recovered it'), 'name, file and lines are real', and the closing 'the index is
incomplete about that file', which restates UNPARSED for a reader who has just been
told the file did not parse.
text: `provenance` ABSENT means doxygen documented the symbol — the normal case. `provenance: 'ast'` means the parser recovered it from source doxygen never emitted, so an empty brief there means UNPARSED, not undocumented.
